To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the fourth amino-acid in N-terminal direction of the cleavage site in the CWSS of C. difficile sortase B substrates plays an essential role for the specific recognition and efficient cleavage by CdSrtB.

the fourth amino acids in the N-terminal directions from cleavage site in the peptide substrates of Cd-SrtA and Cd-SrtB form specific interaction with CdSrtA and CdSrtB, respectively, to configure the peptide substrates for more efficient substrate-specific catalytic cleavage by CdSrtA or CdSrtB.
we have elucidated the molecular basis for the specific recognition of peptide substrates by Clostridum difficile sortase B.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the substrate-specific recognition of sortase and may help the design of inhibitors targeting sortase.
the structural basis for substrate recognition by sortase, which is a critical step for the development of new antibiotics against Gram-positive pathogens.
the structural basis for substrate specificity by Cd-Srt B.

Cd-SrtB recognizes the peptide substrate through a combination of electrostatic and hydrophobic interactions, and the substrate-specific cleavage is mainly determined by the fourth residue in the N-terminal side of the cleavage site.

the fourth residue of PPKTG is the most important determinant of the specificity of PPKTG for Cd-SrtB, and the fourth residue of CWSSs in the substrate proteins is the most important residue in configuring the substrate proteins to allow efficient cleavage by the sortases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the substrate-specificity of Cd-Srt B is determined by a combination of interactions between Cd-SrtB with the CWSS of the peptide substrate and between the CWSS of different peptide substrates.
we have provided a molecular basis of how a sortase enzyme recognizes a peptide substrate and how the substrate-specific cleavage is achieved.
the substrate specificity of Cd-SrtA is mainly determined by the substrate binding site of the enzyme, which is composed of residues from the catalytic pocket and substrate recognition pocket.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the structural basis of substrate recognition by sortase enzymes is more complicated and diverse than previously thought.
despite the high structural similarity among different class sortases, they can still achieve specificity by using different strategies to interact with the peptide substrate.
Cd-SrtB recognizes PPKTG by a combination of specific and nonspecific interactions.
